lens: PartForge: geometry, export, drawings and printables
title: Cold Read
tagline: Read a .scad cold, before any render, and name every SPEC/FLIGHT problem with a line number instead of a count.
pitch: The app's gate learns most declaration problems only after a 10-90 s render: parseSpec returns null for any malformed SPEC, parseFlight silently counts dropped and demoted entries, a declared part whose module does not exist renders nothing after a full compile, and the two dry-run endcap contradictions cost 20-minute CGAL retries although they were visible in the text. Cold Read is a static linter for PartForge files: it parses the comment-carried SPEC and FLIGHT JSON with line-accurate positions, checks that every SPEC part and every FLIGHT module/gauge module has a `module name()`, that main() reaches every declared part through the textual call graph, names each FLIGHT entry parseFlight would drop and why (missing axis, from == to, n outside 1..64, tol <= 0), names each `tol_src: source` without a `tol_ref` (the app demotes these quietly), flags duplicates, category overflow past FLIGHT_CAP 24, hazard and axis vocabulary, tess_tol parameter vs tess_tol_mm mismatch, the parameter block shape and the `--- end parameters ---` sentinel, and runs the app's own flightLint, hobby lint and flightContradictions rules. It never claims a part passes: its last line is always 'text checks only; geometry not checked'. CLI in Node, and a paste-in page that lints as you type.
whyNow: /home/user/Partforge/index.html:2899 parseSpec() returns null on any problem; :4672 parseFlight() returns {malformed:true} or counts `dropped`/`demoted` without naming entries; :4827 flightLint(), :5915 lint(), :4847 flightContradictions() whose comment says 'Both are visible in the text, before a render, and both were spent on 20-minute CGAL retries'. /home/user/Partforge/docs/STATUS.md 'Open, with numbers' item 1: the SPEC part batch re-renders the whole part (24 s on the retainer fixture) so every avoidable retry is expensive. /home/user/Partforge/tests/dryrun/cases.json names the endcap's textual contradictions ('o-ring groove width', 'lightening pocket depth' vs SPEC size 101.5 x 101.5 x 20). The seed's checks ($fn > 128, minkowski, text(), import()) already exist at :5915-5920; the gap is location, naming, module existence and main() reachability.
computes: Inputs: .scad text. Logic: strip block/line comments for code checks while keeping comment lines for SPEC/FLIGHT extraction; JSON.parse with a position-recovering fallback that maps the error offset back to the source line; module table from /^\s*module\s+(\w+)\s*\(/ with line numbers; call graph from identifier( occurrences inside module bodies by brace matching; reachability from main(); FLIGHT entry validation re-implementing parseFlight's acceptance rules and reporting the first failing field per entry; provenance demotion rule (source without ref); duplicates; FLIGHT_CAP; vocabulary regexes FLIGHT_AXIS, TOL_SRC, FLIGHT_HAZARD copied from the DECL excerpt, not retyped; tess_tol param vs FLIGHT tess_tol_mm equality; PARAM_RE compliance before the sentinel; flightLint/lint/flightContradictions executed from the excerpt and merged with line numbers. Output: diagnostics {line, col, severity, code, message, quote}; exit 0/1; JSON or human text.
dataNeeded: Snapshot: tests/templates/*.scad (7 files, 55,228 B total), tests/dryrun/endcap.scad (17,360 B), retainer.scad (10,871 B), retainer-fixed.scad (13,264 B), tests/dryrun/cases.json (2,355 B), tests/flight-templates-cases.json (705 B). Provenance excerpt of DECL-BEGIN..DECL-END (16,204 B, index.html:4646-4859: parseFlight, flightLint, flightContradictions, TOL_SRC, FLIGHT_AXIS, FLIGHT_HAZARD, FLIGHT_CAP) recorded with --sidecar-only. The hobby lint() (index.html:5915-5921) is five lines, quoted in the README with its line numbers rather than excerpted. About 120 KB.
existingOverlap: PartForge ships lint(), flightLint(), parseSpec(), parseFlight(), flightContradictions() and the headless `check` command, all of which run inside or after a render and report counts or null. headless `check` with the cache gives 0.08 s on unchanged source but a changed file pays the render. This differs by running with no engine in milliseconds, by line-numbered diagnostics, by naming dropped and demoted entries, and by the module-existence and main()-reachability checks the app does not do textually. It is explicitly not a gate.
honestyRisks: The danger is a clean lint being read as a pass. Every report ends with the 'geometry not checked' line and the test asserts that retainer.scad, whose real failure is geometric (a lip unioned into a pocket, cases.json), lints with zero errors and that line present. A second danger is a second truth about what parseFlight accepts: the acceptance rules are executed from the DECL excerpt and the linter's named lists are asserted equal in count to parseFlight's dropped/demoted counters on every fixture, so a divergence fails the test. Vocabulary constants are imported from the excerpt, never retyped. Line mapping of JSON errors is best effort and labelled [Likely] where the parser recovers.
testPlan: node --test: (1) all 7 templates: 0 errors, 0 warnings, and flightLint from the excerpt also returns [] for each. (2) endcap.scad: diagnostics include contradictions for 'o-ring groove width' and 'lightening pocket depth' with the SPEC size 101.5 x 101.5 x 20 quoted and line numbers inside the FLIGHT block; counts of named dropped/demoted entries equal parseFlight(code).dropped and .demoted. (3) retainer.scad: 0 textual errors and the footer line present (refusal to overclaim). (4) Mutations of centering-ring.scad: rename `module ring()` to `rng` yields 'SPEC part "ring" has no module' and 'main() does not reach ring'; delete a tol_ref yields a named demotion at its line; set a hole n to 0 yields a named drop with reason 'n outside 1..64'; add `$fn = 200;` yields the app's global-$fn message and the $fn > 128 warning; add `text("A")` yields the text() warning. (5) Malformed JSON (a trailing comma) reports the line of the comma. (6) Page smoke at 390 px with the paste box and diagnostics list.
landing: PartForge headless: `cli.mjs lint part.scad` and an MCP tool `lint_part` returning the standard envelope with confidence 'derived'; in the browser, inline diagnostics beside the code pane before Generate re-renders. To ship: the rule set must be generated from index.html by build.mjs (wrapping parseSpec/parseFlight/flightLint and adding line mapping) rather than kept as this re-implementation, so headless and browser cannot disagree; and the flight doctrine's retry prompt could quote a lint finding before spending a render.
notes: Verified parseFlight counts dropped/demoted without naming entries and flightContradictions' comment about 20-minute CGAL retries. Line-numbered pre-render lint saves real time; footer refuses to overclaim.
